takeaway: The posterior wall of the inguinal canal is mainly transversalis fascia, reinforced medially by the conjoint tendon. The pectineal ligament belongs to the femoral canal.

lines.text: The inguinal canal runs for 4–6 cm, from the deep ring to the superficial ring.
lines.say: The inguinal canal runs for four to six centimetres, from the deep ring to the superficial ring.

lines.text: Its posterior border is mainly the transversalis fascia.
Medially, that back wall is reinforced by the conjoint tendon.
In front lies the external oblique aponeurosis, reinforced laterally by internal oblique fibres.
The floor is the inguinal ligament,
and the roof is the arching fibres of internal oblique and transversus abdominis, the conjoint tendon.
Beware the pectineal ligament: it forms the posterior border of the femoral canal.
lines.say: (clears throat) Beware the pectineal ligament: it forms the posterior border of the femoral canal.

lines.text: So the answer is the transversalis fascia.
